<style id="pag-slider-style-inline-css">

    .pag-slider-wrap{
        max-width:1290px;
        margin:0 auto 40px auto;
        font-family:inherit;
    }
    .pag-slider{
        overflow-x:auto;
        overflow-y:hidden;
        width:100%;
        scroll-behavior:smooth;
        -webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch;
    }
    .pag-slider::-webkit-scrollbar{display:none}
    .pag-track{display:flex}
    .pag-item{
        flex:0 0 20%;
        padding:0 8px;
        box-sizing:border-box;
        display:flex;
        flex-direction:column;
    }
    .pag-image-link img{width:100%;height:auto;display:block}
    .pag-image-placeholder{width:100%;padding-top:75%;background:#f5f5f5}
    .pag-name{
        display:block;
        background:#f5f5f5;
        padding:12px 14px;
        font-size:14px;
        color:#000;
        text-decoration:none;
    }
    .pag-name:hover{text-decoration:underline}
    .pag-nav{display:flex;justify-content:center;margin-top:24px}
    .pag-nav-pill{
        display:flex;
        background:#f5f5f5;
        border-radius:999px;
        overflow:hidden;
        border:1px solid #e3e3e3;
        box-shadow:0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.6) inset;
    }
    .pag-prev,.pag-next{
        width:60px;
        height:38px;
        border:0;
        background:transparent;
        display:flex;
        align-items:center;
        justify-content:center;
        cursor:pointer;
        font-size:18px;
        line-height:1;
        color:#666;
        padding:0;
    }
    .pag-prev{border-right:1px solid #e3e3e3}
    .pag-prev::before{content:"\2190"}
    .pag-next::before{content:"\2192"}
    .pag-prev:hover,.pag-next:hover{color:#333}
    .pag-prev:disabled,.pag-next:disabled{opacity:.4;cursor:default}
    @media (max-width:1024px){
        .pag-item{flex:0 0 33.3333%}
    }
    @media (max-width:768px){
        .pag-item{flex:0 0 80%}
        .pag-nav{margin-top:18px}
    }

<style id="mega-menu-styles-inline-css">

            .mega-menu-container {
                position: relative;
            }
            .mega-menu-header {
                display: flex;
                justify-content: flex-start;
                align-items: center;
                margin-bottom: 10px;
            }
            .mega-menu-title {
                font-size: 14px;
                font-weight: 700;
                color: #333;
                margin: 0;
            }
            .mega-menu-view-all {
                display: inline-block;
                color: #197e3c;
                text-decoration: none;
                font-weight: 600;
                font-size: 14px;
                transition: color 0.3s ease;
                padding: 0 10px;
            }
            .mega-menu-view-all:hover {
                color: #197e3c;
            }
            .mega-menu-content {
                display: flex;
                gap: 0;
                position: static;
            }
            .mega-menu-categories {
                flex: 0 0 280px;
                position: relative;
                z-index: 10;
            }
            .mega-menu-category-item {
                padding: 5px 0px;
                transition: all 0.3s ease;
                color: #333;
                font-weight: 600;
                font-size: 13px;
                position: relative;
            }
            .mega-menu-category-item.has-children {
                cursor: pointer;
            }
            .mega-menu-category-item a {
                color: #333;
                text-decoration: none;
                display: block;
            }
            .mega-menu-category-item a:hover {
                color: #197e3c;
            }
            .mega-menu-category-item::before {
                content: "";
                position: absolute;
                left: -10px;
                top: 50%;
                transform: translateY(-50%);
                width: 3px;
                height: 1em;
                background-color: transparent;
                transition: background-color 0.3s ease;
            }
            /* 只有激活状态才显示绿色，移除hover状态避免冲突 */
            .mega-menu-category-item.active::before {
                background-color: #197e3c;
            }
            .mega-menu-category-item.active {
                color: #197e3c !important;
            }
            /* 非激活状态的悬停效果 */
            .mega-menu-category-item:not(.active):hover {
                color: #197e3c;
            }
            .mega-menu-category-item:not(.active):hover::before {
                background-color: #197e3c;
            }
            .mega-menu-dropdown {
                position: fixed;
                left: auto;
                top: auto;
                min-width: 900px;
                height: 400px;
                background: #fff;
                padding: 30px;
                padding-left: 33px;
                z-index: 100;
                display: none;
                margin-left: -40px;
                margin-top: 0;
                box-sizing: border-box;
                overflow: hidden;
            }
            .mega-menu-dropdown::before {
                content: "";
                position: absolute;
                left: 0;
                top: 50%;
                transform: translateY(-50%);
                width: 3px;
                height: 300px;
                background-color: #197e3c;
            }
            .mega-menu-dropdown.active {
                display: block;
            }
            .mega-menu-dropdown-content {
                display: none;
            }
            .mega-menu-dropdown-content.active {
                display: block;
                animation: fadeIn 0.3s ease;
            }
            @keyframes fadeIn {
                from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-10px); }
                to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
            }
            .mega-menu-dropdown-header {
                display: flex;
                justify-content: flex-start;
                align-items: center;
                margin-bottom: 20px;
                gap: 10px;
            }
            .mega-menu-dropdown-title {
                font-size: 14px;
                font-weight: 700;
                color: #333;
                margin: 0;
            }
            .mega-menu-dropdown-view-all {
                display: inline-block;
                color: #197e3c;
                text-decoration: none;
                font-weight: 600;
                font-size: 14px;
                transition: color 0.3s ease;
            }
            .mega-menu-dropdown-view-all:hover {
                color: #197e3c;
            }
            .mega-menu-items-grid {
                column-count: 2;
                column-gap: 30px;
            }
            .mega-menu-item {
                padding: 8px 0;
                break-inside: avoid;
                page-break-inside: avoid;
            }
            .mega-menu-item a {
                color: #333;
                text-decoration: none;
                transition: all 0.3s ease;
                display: block;
                font-size: 13px;
                position: relative;
            }
            .mega-menu-item a::before {
                content: "";
                position: absolute;
                left: -10px;
                top: 50%;
                transform: translateY(-50%);
                width: 3px;
                height: 1em;
                background-color: transparent;
                transition: background-color 0.3s ease;
            }
            .mega-menu-item a:hover::before {
                background-color: #197e3c;
            }
            .mega-menu-item a:hover {
                color: #197e3c;
                text-decoration: underline;
            }
            .mega-menu-item .count {
                color: #999;
                font-size: 12px;
                margin-left: 5px;
            }
            @media (max-width: 992px) {
                .mega-menu-content {
                    flex-direction: column;
                }
                .mega-menu-categories {
                    flex: 1;
                }
                .mega-menu-dropdown {
                    position: relative;
                    left: 0;
                    min-width: auto;
                    box-shadow: none;
                    padding: 20px 0;
                }
                .mega-menu-items-grid {
                    grid-template-columns: 1fr;
                }
            }
            @media (max-width: 768px) {
                .mega-menu-header {
                    flex-direction: row;
                    align-items: center;
                    gap: 10px;
                }
                .mega-menu-title {
                    font-size: 14px;
                }
                .mega-menu-dropdown {
                    display: none !important;
                }
            }
        
/*# sourceURL=mega-menu-styles-inline-css */

<style id="pcsb-style-inline-css">
.elementor .pcsb, .pcsb{box-sizing:border-box}
.elementor .pcsb *, .pcsb *{box-sizing:inherit}
.elementor .pcsb ul, .pcsb ul{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0}

.pcsb{background:#F5F5F5; display:block}
.pcsb-hd{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:8px;padding:14px 12px}
.pcsb-title{font-weight:700;font-size:16px;margin:0;flex:1;min-width:0;line-height:1.3;color:#111}
.pcsb-icon{width:18px;height:18px;flex:0 0 18px;margin-left:auto}

.pcsb-list,.pcsb-sub{margin:0;padding:0}
.pcsb-li{border-top:1px solid #E5E5E5}
.pcsb-row{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;padding:14px 12px}

.pcsb-link{flex:1;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;text-decoration:none}
.pcsb-txt{font-size:14px;color:#222;margin:0;flex:1;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;white-space:nowrap}
.pcsb-arrow{width:18px;height:18px;flex:0 0 18px}

.pcsb-toggle{background:transparent;border:0;cursor:pointer;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;width:24px;height:24px;margin-left:4px}
.pcsb-toggle svg{width:18px;height:18px;transition:transform .2s}

.pcsb-link:hover .pcsb-txt{color:#000}
.pcsb-row:hover{background:#EEEEEE}
.pcsb-li.active>.pcsb-row,.pcsb-li.active>.pcsb-row:hover{background:#1A7E3B}
.pcsb-li.active .pcsb-txt{color:#fff}
.pcsb-li.active .pcsb-arrow path{stroke:#fff}

.pcsb-sub{display:none}
.pcsb-li.open>.pcsb-sub{display:block}
.pcsb-li.open>.pcsb-row .pcsb-toggle svg{transform:rotate(180deg)}
.pcsb-sub .pcsb-li{border-top:1px solid #EDEDED}
.pcsb-sub .pcsb-row{padding:14px 12px 14px 24px}
.pcsb-sub .pcsb-sub .pcsb-row{padding-left:36px}
.pcsb-li.ancestor>.pcsb-row{background:transparent}

@media (max-width:767.98px){
  .pcsb-hd{padding:14px 12px}
}
/*# sourceURL=pcsb-style-inline-css */
</style>

jQuery(document).ready(function($) {
                $('.mega-menu-container').each(function() {
                    var container = $(this);
                    var categoryItems = container.find('.mega-menu-category-item');
                    var dropdownContents = container.find('.mega-menu-dropdown-content');
                    var dropdown = container.find('.mega-menu-dropdown');
                    var categoriesDiv = container.find('.mega-menu-categories');
                    
                    // 清理所有状态的函数
                    function clearAllStates() {
                        categoryItems.removeClass('active');
                        dropdownContents.removeClass('active');
                        dropdown.removeClass('active');
                    }
                    
                    // 鼠标进入一级菜单项
                    categoryItems.on('mouseenter', function() {
                        var $this = $(this);
                        var index = $this.data('index');
                        
                        // 立即清理所有状态
                        clearAllStates();
                        
                        // 如果有子分类，显示下拉菜单
                        if ($this.hasClass('has-children')) {
                            // 延迟一小段时间确保状态清理完成
                            setTimeout(function() {
                                $this.addClass('active');
                                dropdown.addClass('active');
                                container.find('.mega-menu-dropdown-content[data-index="' + index + '"]').addClass('active');
                                
                                // 计算并设置dropdown位置
                                var targetContainer = $('.elementor-2754 .elementor-element.elementor-element-007d99b');
                                
                                if (targetContainer.length > 0) {
                                    var targetTop = targetContainer.offset().top;
                                    dropdown.css('top', targetTop + 'px');
                                } else {
                                    var menuaContainer = $('.menua');
                                    if (menuaContainer.length > 0) {
                                        dropdown.css('top', menuaContainer.offset().top + 'px');
                                    } else {
                                        dropdown.css('top', container.find('.mega-menu-content').offset().top + 'px');
                                    }
                                }
                                
                                // 设置左边位置
                                var categoriesRight = categoriesDiv.offset().left + categoriesDiv.outerWidth();
                                dropdown.css('left', (categoriesRight - 40) + 'px');
                            }, 10);
                        }
                    });
                    
                    // 鼠标离开菜单项
                    categoryItems.on('mouseleave', function() {
                        // 短暂延迟，给用户时间移动到下拉菜单
                        setTimeout(function() {
                            if (!dropdown.is(':hover') && !categoriesDiv.is(':hover')) {
                                clearAllStates();
                            }
                        }, 100);
                    });
                    
                    // 鼠标进入下拉菜单区域
                    dropdown.on('mouseenter', function() {
                        // 保持当前状态
                    });
                    
                    // 鼠标离开下拉菜单区域
                    dropdown.on('mouseleave', function() {
                        clearAllStates();
                    });
                    
                    // 鼠标离开整个菜单容器
                    container.on('mouseleave', function() {
                        clearAllStates();
                    });
                });

            jQuery(document).ready(function($) {
                $('.aerospace-showcase-module').each(function() {
                    var module = $(this);
                    var cards = module.find('.aerospace-card');
                    var currentIndex = 0;
                    var autoplayInterval;
                    var isHovering = false;
                    
                    if (cards.length === 0) return;
                    
                    function startAutoplay() {
                        stopAutoplay(); // 先清除旧的定时器
                        autoplayInterval = setInterval(function() {
                            if (!isHovering) { 
                                flipNextCard(); 
                            }
                        }, 3000);
                    }
                    
                    function stopAutoplay() { 
                        if (autoplayInterval) {
                            clearInterval(autoplayInterval); 
                        }
                    }
                    
                    function flipNextCard() {
                        // 隐藏当前卡片内容
                        cards.eq(currentIndex).removeClass('active');
                        
                        // 移到下一张
                        currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % cards.length;
                        
                        // 显示新卡片内容
                        cards.eq(currentIndex).addClass('active');
                    }
                    
                    // 鼠标悬停时显示内容
                    cards.on('mouseenter', function() {
                        var hoveredIndex = cards.index(this);
                        
                        // 隐藏之前轮播激活的卡片
                        cards.eq(currentIndex).removeClass('active');
                        
                        // 显示悬停的卡片
                        $(this).addClass('active');
                        
                        // 更新当前索引为悬停的卡片
                        currentIndex = hoveredIndex;
                        
                        // 标记为悬停状态
                        isHovering = true;
                        
                        // 重启轮播定时器（从悬停的卡片开始）
                        startAutoplay();
                    });
                    
                    cards.on('mouseleave', function() { 
                        isHovering = false;
                        // 鼠标离开后，保持当前卡片激活状态，轮播会继续
                    });
                    
                    // 启动自动播放
                    startAutoplay();
                    // 第一张卡片立即显示
                    setTimeout(function() {
                        cards.eq(0).addClass('active');
                    }, 500);
                    
                    // 页面可见性变化时控制自动播放
                    $(document).on('visibilitychange', function() {
                        if (document.hidden) { 
                            stopAutoplay(); 
                        } else { 
                            startAutoplay(); 
                        }
                    });
                });
            });

<p>When the <strong><a href="https://pcbsync.com/raspberry-pi/" data-wpel-link="internal">Raspberry Pi</a> Compute Module 4</strong> landed on my workbench in late 2020, it represented everything I’d wanted from an embedded Linux platform for commercial product development. The previous compute modules were capable, but the <strong>CM4</strong> brought a fundamentally new architecture that finally addressed the limitations holding back serious industrial applications. After designing multiple carrier boards and deploying dozens of <strong>raspberry pi cm4</strong> units across various projects, I can share practical insights that go beyond the marketing specifications.</p>



<p>This comprehensive guide covers everything developers need to know about the <a href="https://pcbsync.com/raspberry-pi/" data-wpel-link="internal"><u>Raspberry Pi</u></a> Compute Module 4, from hardware specifications and carrier board design to programming the eMMC and selecting the right variant for your application. Whether you’re prototyping on the official IO board or designing a custom carrier for production, this resource will accelerate your development process.</p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>What Is the Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4?</strong><strong></strong></h2>



<p>The <strong>Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4</strong> is a system-on-module (SoM) that packages the core functionality of the <a href="https://pcbsync.com/raspberry-pi-4/" data-wpel-link="internal">Raspberry Pi 4</a> Model B into a compact form factor designed for integration into custom hardware. Unlike the consumer-oriented Pi 4B with its fixed ports and connectors, the <strong>CM4</strong> exposes all interfaces through two high-density 100-pin mezzanine connectors, giving hardware designers complete freedom in implementing only the features their application requires.</p>



<p>Released in October 2020, the <strong>raspberry pi compute module 4</strong> marked a significant departure from previous compute modules. Earlier generations (CM1, CM3, CM3+) used the DDR2 SODIMM form factor familiar from laptop memory modules. The CM4 abandoned this approach for a more compact design measuring just 55mm × 40mm, while simultaneously adding capabilities impossible in the previous form factor.</p>



<p>The module is specifically designed for industrial and commercial applications including digital signage, thin clients, network appliances, robotics, and process automation. Raspberry Pi commits to keeping the CM4 in production until at least January 2031, providing the long-term availability that commercial products require.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>CM4 Hardware Specifications</strong><strong></strong></h2>



<p>Understanding the complete hardware capabilities helps you evaluate whether the <strong>raspberry pi cm4</strong> meets your project requirements.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Processor and Memory</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<figure class="wp-block-table"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><tbody><tr><td><strong>Component</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>Specification</strong><strong></strong></td></tr><tr><td>SoC</td><td>Broadcom BCM2711</td></tr><tr><td>CPU</td><td>Quad-core Cortex-A72 (ARM v8) 64-bit @ 1.5GHz</td></tr><tr><td>GPU</td><td>VideoCore VI @ 500MHz</td></tr><tr><td>RAM Options</td><td>1GB, 2GB, 4GB, or 8GB LPDDR4-3200</td></tr><tr><td>RAM Bandwidth</td><td>4266MT/s (32-bit bus)</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>



<p>The BCM2711 delivers approximately twice the performance of the BCM2837B0 used in the CM3+, thanks to the more capable Cortex-A72 cores. This isn’t just a clock speed bump; the A72 architecture includes larger caches, improved branch prediction, and better memory handling that translate to real-world performance gains in compute-intensive applications.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Storage Options</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<figure class="wp-block-table"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><tbody><tr><td><strong>Variant</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>eMMC Capacity</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>Boot Options</strong><strong></strong></td></tr><tr><td>CM4Lite</td><td>None</td><td>microSD, USB, Network</td></tr><tr><td>CM4 8GB</td><td>8GB eMMC</td><td>eMMC, USB, Network</td></tr><tr><td>CM4 16GB</td><td>16GB eMMC</td><td>eMMC, USB, Network</td></tr><tr><td>CM4 32GB</td><td>32GB eMMC</td><td>eMMC, USB, Network</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>



<p>The CM4Lite variants omit on-board storage entirely, requiring a carrier board with microSD slot or alternative boot mechanism. The eMMC versions include industrial-grade flash storage soldered directly to the module, eliminating the reliability concerns associated with SD cards in demanding environments.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Connectivity and Interfaces</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<figure class="wp-block-table"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><tbody><tr><td><strong>Interface</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>Specification</strong><strong></strong></td></tr><tr><td>Gigabit Ethernet</td><td>Native PHY with IEEE 1588 support</td></tr><tr><td>WiFi</td><td>2.4GHz/5.0GHz 802.11 b/g/n/ac (optional)</td></tr><tr><td>Bluetooth</td><td>5.0, BLE (optional)</td></tr><tr><td>USB</td><td>1× USB 2.0 port</td></tr><tr><td>PCIe</td><td>Gen 2.0 x1 lane</td></tr><tr><td>HDMI</td><td>2× HDMI 2.0 (up to 4Kp60)</td></tr><tr><td>Camera/Display</td><td>2× <a href="https://pcbsync.com/xilinx-mipi-ip/" data-wpel-link="internal">MIPI CSI-2</a>, 2× MIPI DSI</td></tr><tr><td>GPIO</td><td>28 user GPIO pins</td></tr><tr><td>I2C</td><td>Multiple buses available</td></tr><tr><td>SPI</td><td>Multiple buses available</td></tr><tr><td>UART</td><td>Multiple UARTs available</td></tr><tr><td>PWM</td><td>Available on GPIO</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Physical Specifications</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<figure class="wp-block-table"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><tbody><tr><td><strong>Parameter</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>Value</strong><strong></strong></td></tr><tr><td>Dimensions</td><td>55mm × 40mm</td></tr><tr><td>Module Height</td><td>4.7mm (flat), 5.078mm/6.578mm with standoffs</td></tr><tr><td>Connectors</td><td>2× 100-pin Hirose DF40C-100DS-0.4V</td></tr><tr><td>Weight</td><td>Approximately 14g</td></tr><tr><td>Operating Temperature</td><td>0°C to +80°C (standard), -20°C to +85°C (industrial)</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>CM4 Variants and Pricing</strong><strong></strong></h2>



<p>With 32 distinct SKUs available, selecting the right <strong>raspberry pi compute module 4</strong> variant requires understanding your project’s actual needs. The combinations span RAM capacity (1/2/4/8 GB), storage capacity (none/8/16/32 GB eMMC), and wireless connectivity (with or without WiFi/Bluetooth).</p>

<p>Prices shown are MSRP in USD. The wireless module adds $5 to any configuration. Each storage tier adds $5 to the base price.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Choosing the Right Variant</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p><strong>For prototyping and development</strong>: Start with a 4GB RAM, 32GB eMMC, wireless-enabled module. This provides flexibility during development when requirements may change.</p>



<p><strong>For headless servers and network appliances</strong>: Consider 2GB or 4GB RAM with no wireless (use Gigabit Ethernet instead) and 8GB or 16GB eMMC. The $40-55 range offers excellent value.</p>



<p><strong>For digital signage and media players</strong>: Choose 2GB or 4GB RAM with storage sized for your content. Wireless is optional depending on deployment location.</p>



<p><strong>For edge AI and compute-intensive applications</strong>: The 8GB RAM variant becomes essential when running TensorFlow, OpenCV, or similar frameworks. Pair with NVMe storage via PCIe for maximum performance.</p>



<p><strong>For cost-sensitive production</strong>: The $25 base model (1GB RAM, no eMMC, no wireless) makes sense only for extremely constrained applications. Most projects benefit from at least 2GB RAM.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>The CM4 IO Board</strong><strong></strong></h2>



<p>The official Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 IO Board provides access to all CM4 interfaces through standard connectors, serving as both a development platform and reference design for custom carrier boards.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>IO Board Features</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<figure class="wp-block-table"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><tbody><tr><td><strong>Feature</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>Implementation</strong><strong></strong></td></tr><tr><td>Power Input</td><td>7.5V-28V barrel jack, supports industrial 12V/24V systems</td></tr><tr><td>HDMI</td><td>2× full-size HDMI 2.0 ports</td></tr><tr><td>USB</td><td>2× USB 2.0 Type-A ports (via hub)</td></tr><tr><td>Ethernet</td><td>Gigabit RJ45 jack</td></tr><tr><td>microSD</td><td>Slot for CM4Lite variants</td></tr><tr><td>PCIe</td><td>x1 slot for expansion cards</td></tr><tr><td>Camera</td><td>2× 22-pin FFC connectors (15-pin camera adapter included)</td></tr><tr><td>Display</td><td>2× 22-pin FFC connectors</td></tr><tr><td>GPIO</td><td>40-pin header (Pi 4 compatible)</td></tr><tr><td>RTC</td><td>Battery backup connector</td></tr><tr><td>PoE</td><td>Header for <a href="https://pcbsync.com/raspberry-pi-poe-hat/" data-wpel-link="internal">PoE HAT</a></td></tr><tr><td>Fan</td><td>PWM-controlled fan header</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>



<p>The IO board’s PCIe slot deserves special attention. While the Pi 4B routes its single PCIe lane to the VL805 USB 3.0 controller chip, the <strong>CM4</strong> exposes this lane directly. This enables connecting NVMe SSDs, network interface cards, SATA controllers, or specialized hardware like the Google Coral TPU. <h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Using the IO Board for Development</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>For most developers, the IO board provides everything needed to evaluate the CM4 and develop software before committing to custom hardware. The board’s comprehensive breakout of all signals also makes it invaluable for debugging custom carrier board designs.</p>



<p>One important consideration: the IO board’s size (160mm × 90mm) and connector selection prioritize development convenience over production suitability. Custom carrier boards typically reduce dimensions by 50-80% by including only necessary interfaces.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Flashing the CM4 eMMC Storage</strong><strong></strong></h2>



<p>Programming the embedded flash storage requires a different workflow than the familiar microSD card approach. The process involves booting the CM4 into a special USB mass storage mode that exposes the eMMC as an external drive.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Hardware Setup for eMMC Flashing</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>Before connecting power, configure the carrier board for programming mode:</p>



<ol class="wp-block-list">
<li>Install a jumper on the J2 header (labeled “Fit jumper to disable eMMC Boot” on the IO board)</li>



<li>Connect a USB cable from your computer to the “USB Slave” micro USB port on the IO board</li>



<li>Connect power to the IO board</li>
</ol>



<p>The CM4 will power on (D1 LED illuminates) but will not boot from eMMC due to the jumper. Instead, it waits for the host computer to initiate the boot process.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Installing rpiboot</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>The rpiboot utility communicates with the CM4’s boot ROM to expose the eMMC as a mass storage device.</p>



<p><strong>On Linux or <a href="https://pcbsync.com/raspberry-pi-os/" data-wpel-link="internal">Raspberry Pi OS</a>:</strong></p>



<p>sudo <a href="https://pcbsync.com/aperture-file-apt/" data-wpel-link="internal">apt</a> install libusb-1.0-0-dev</p>



<p>git clone –depth=1 https://github.com/raspberrypi/usbboot</p>



<p>cd usbboot</p>



<p>make</p>



<p>sudo ./rpiboot</p>



<p><strong>On macOS:</strong></p>



<p>brew install libusb pkg-config</p>



<p>git clone –depth=1 https://github.com/raspberrypi/usbboot</p>



<p>cd usbboot</p>



<p>make</p>



<p>sudo ./rpiboot</p>



<p><strong>On Windows:</strong> Download and run the pre-built installer from the usbboot repository’s win32 directory. The installer configures necessary drivers automatically.</p>

<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Enabling USB Ports</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>An important post-installation step often catches newcomers: the <strong>CM4</strong> ships with USB disabled by default to save power in embedded applications. To enable USB ports, add the following line to /boot/config.txt:</p>



<p>dtoverlay=dwc2,dr_mode=host</p>



<p>Alternatively, for the IO board specifically:</p>



<p>dtoverlay=cm4-io-board</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Designing Custom Carrier Boards</strong><strong></strong></h2>



<p>Creating a custom carrier board transforms the <strong>raspberry pi cm4</strong> from a development platform into a production-ready solution tailored to your application’s exact requirements.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Essential Design Resources</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>Raspberry Pi provides comprehensive design files to accelerate carrier board development:</p>



<figure class="wp-block-table"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><tbody><tr><td><strong>Resource</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>Description</strong><strong></strong></td></tr><tr><td>CM4 Datasheet</td><td>Complete electrical specifications and interface details</td></tr><tr><td>CM4IO KiCad Files</td><td>Schematic and PCB files for the official IO board</td></tr><tr><td>CM4 Product Brief</td><td>Overview document with key specifications</td></tr><tr><td>Hardware Design Guide</td><td>Carrier board design recommendations</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>



<p>The official IO board KiCad files deserve special attention. They include verified footprints for the Hirose connectors, tested routing for high-speed signals, and working reference designs for every interface. Starting from these files rather than creating components from scratch saves weeks of development time.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Connector Considerations</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>The dual 100-pin Hirose DF40C connectors (or compatible alternatives from Panasonic, JAE, or Amphenol) require careful <a href="https://pcbsync.com/pcb-design/" data-wpel-link="internal">PCB design</a>:</p>

<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Minimal Carrier Board Design</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>A bare-minimum carrier board requires surprisingly few components:</p>



<ol class="wp-block-list">
<li>Two 100-pin connectors</li>



<li>5V power input with appropriate filtering</li>



<li>Power indicator LED</li>



<li>Activity indicator LED</li>
</ol>



<p>This configuration supports CM4 variants with onboard eMMC and WiFi, providing a functional system in the smallest possible footprint. The CM4 handles all power regulation internally, requiring only a clean 5V supply.</p>

<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Adding PCIe NVMe Support</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>The PCIe interface enables significantly faster storage than eMMC or SD cards provide. Implementing an M.2 slot requires:</p>



<figure class="wp-block-table"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><tbody><tr><td><strong>Signal</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>Notes</strong><strong></strong></td></tr><tr><td>PCIe_TX+/-</td><td>Transmit differential pair, 100Ω impedance</td></tr><tr><td>PCIe_RX+/-</td><td>Receive differential pair, 100Ω impedance</td></tr><tr><td>PCIe_CLK_REQ#</td><td>Clock request from device</td></tr><tr><td>PCIe_RESET#</td><td>Reset signal</td></tr><tr><td>REFCLK+/-</td><td>100MHz reference clock (some designs omit, using device internal clock)</td></tr><tr><td>3.3V Power</td><td>M.2 specification requires 3.3V supply</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>



<p>The CM4 includes AC coupling capacitors on the transmit pair, so your carrier board needs capacitors only on signals originating from the M.2 device. Most successful designs place these as close to the mezzanine connector as possible.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Power Considerations</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>The <strong>CM4</strong> simplifies carrier board power design compared to previous compute modules:</p>



<figure class="wp-block-table"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><tbody><tr><td><strong>Power Rail</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>CM4 Consumption</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>Notes</strong><strong></strong></td></tr><tr><td>5V Input</td><td>1.4A typical (idle ~400mA)</td><td>Single supply, CM4 generates internal rails</td></tr><tr><td>3.3V Output</td><td>Up to 600mA available</td><td>For carrier board peripherals</td></tr><tr><td>1.8V Output</td><td>Up to 600mA available</td><td>For carrier board peripherals</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>



<p>The 5V input must be clean and stable. Include appropriate bulk capacitance (100-470µF) near the connectors and high-frequency decoupling (100nF ceramic) distributed across the power plane.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Third-Party Carrier Boards</strong><strong></strong></h2>



<p>The CM4 ecosystem includes numerous carrier boards from third parties, each targeting specific use cases.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Popular Carrier Board Comparison</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<figure class="wp-block-table"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><tbody><tr><td><strong>Board</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>Key Features</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>Best For</strong><strong></strong></td></tr><tr><td>Official IO Board</td><td>Full feature breakout, PCIe slot</td><td>Development, prototyping</td></tr><tr><td>Waveshare CM4-IO-BASE-A</td><td>Compact, dual cameras, M.2 2242</td><td>Space-constrained projects</td></tr><tr><td>TOFU by Oratek</td><td>9cm square, M.2 B-key, industrial focus</td><td>Industrial applications</td></tr><tr><td>Piunora</td><td><a href="https://pcbsync.com/arduino/" data-wpel-link="internal">Arduino</a> form factor, M.2, Qwiic</td><td>Maker projects, prototyping</td></tr><tr><td>Compute Blade</td><td>Rack-mount, PoE+, NVMe</td><td>Server clusters, home labs</td></tr><tr><td>Gumstix Development Board</td><td>Full IO, AI accelerator support</td><td>Edge AI development</td></tr><tr><td>Seeed <a href="https://pcbsync.com/reterminal/" data-wpel-link="internal">reTerminal</a></td><td>Integrated display, touch, GPIO</td><td>HMI applications</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>



<p>When selecting a third-party carrier board, verify that it exposes the specific interfaces your application requires. Many compact boards omit features like the second HDMI, camera interfaces, or full GPIO header to achieve smaller dimensions.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>CM4 vs Previous Compute Modules</strong><strong></strong></h2>



<p>Understanding how the <strong>raspberry pi cm4</strong> compares to earlier generations helps evaluate upgrade paths for existing products.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Generation Comparison</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<figure class="wp-block-table"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><tbody><tr><td><strong>Feature</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>CM1</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>CM3/CM3+</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>CM4</strong><strong></strong></td></tr><tr><td>CPU</td><td>BCM2835</td><td>BCM2837B0</td><td>BCM2711</td></tr><tr><td>Cores</td><td>1× ARM1176</td><td>4× Cortex-A53</td><td>4× Cortex-A72</td></tr><tr><td>Clock</td><td>700MHz</td><td>1.2GHz</td><td>1.5GHz</td></tr><tr><td>RAM</td><td>512MB</td><td>1GB</td><td>1-8GB</td></tr><tr><td>eMMC</td><td>4GB</td><td>0-32GB</td><td>0-32GB</td></tr><tr><td>Form Factor</td><td>DDR2 SODIMM</td><td>DDR2 SODIMM</td><td>Dual 100-pin</td></tr><tr><td>Gigabit Ethernet</td><td>No</td><td>No</td><td>Yes (native)</td></tr><tr><td>WiFi/BT</td><td>No</td><td>No</td><td>Optional</td></tr><tr><td>PCIe</td><td>No</td><td>No</td><td>Yes (x1 Gen 2)</td></tr><tr><td>USB 2.0</td><td>1</td><td>1</td><td>1</td></tr><tr><td>HDMI</td><td>1</td><td>1</td><td>2</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>



<p>The shift away from the DDR2 SODIMM form factor means <a href="https://pcbsync.com/best-cm4-carrier-boards/" data-wpel-link="internal">CM4 carrier boards</a> are incompatible with earlier compute modules. However, Raspberry Pi released the CM4S specifically for applications requiring backward compatibility, offering CM4 performance in the legacy SODIMM form factor (without WiFi/Bluetooth support).</p>

<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Digital Signage</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>The dual 4K HDMI outputs support video walls and high-resolution displays. The eMMC storage eliminates SD card failures that plague 24/7 signage deployments. Network boot capability allows centralized content management across large installations.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Network Appliances</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>Native Gigabit Ethernet with IEEE 1588 precision timing support enables network monitoring, firewall, and router applications. The PCIe slot can accommodate additional network interfaces, NVMe caching, or hardware acceleration cards.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Edge Computing and AI</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>The 8GB RAM variant combined with the Google Coral TPU (connected via PCIe or USB) creates a capable edge AI platform. Applications include real-time video analytics, anomaly detection, and sensor data processing.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Robotics and Automation</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>The extensive GPIO, multiple I2C/SPI buses, and camera interfaces support complex robotic systems. The compact form factor fits within space-constrained enclosures, while the processing power handles computer vision and path planning algorithms.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Medical and Scientific Instruments</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>The -20°C to +85°C extended temperature range (on industrial variants) meets requirements for laboratory and field equipment. Long-term availability commitments satisfy medical device certification requirements.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Software and Operating System Support</strong><strong></strong></h2>



<p>The <strong>CM4</strong> runs the same software ecosystem as the Pi 4B, with some hardware-specific considerations.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Supported Operating Systems</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<figure class="wp-block-table"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><tbody><tr><td><strong>OS</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>Status</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>Notes</strong><strong></strong></td></tr><tr><td>Raspberry Pi OS (32-bit)</td><td>Full support</td><td>Official, Debian-based</td></tr><tr><td>Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit)</td><td>Full support</td><td>Recommended for 8GB RAM</td></tr><tr><td>Ubuntu Server</td><td>Full support</td><td>20.04 LTS, 22.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS</td></tr><tr><td>Ubuntu Desktop</td><td>Full support</td><td>Requires adequate RAM</td></tr><tr><td>Fedora</td><td>Community support</td><td>ARM SIG builds</td></tr><tr><td>Buildroot</td><td>Full support</td><td>Custom minimal systems</td></tr><tr><td>Yocto</td><td>Full support</td><td>Production embedded Linux</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Boot Configuration</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>The CM4’s boot process differs slightly from the Pi 4B due to the eMMC option and industrial use cases:</p>



<figure class="wp-block-table"><table class="has-fixed-layout"><tbody><tr><td><strong>Boot Source</strong><strong></strong></td><td><strong>Configuration</strong><strong></strong></td></tr><tr><td>eMMC (default)</td><td>No configuration needed on eMMC variants</td></tr><tr><td>microSD</td><td>CM4Lite only, automatic fallback</td></tr><tr><td>USB</td><td>Enable in EEPROM bootloader configuration</td></tr><tr><td>Network (PXE)</td><td>Enable in EEPROM bootloader configuration</td></tr><tr><td>NVMe</td><td>Enable in EEPROM, requires bootloader update</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>



<p>To modify boot order or enable NVMe boot, use the rpi-eeprom-config utility to update the bootloader configuration stored in the CM4’s EEPROM.</p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Frequently Asked Questions</strong><strong></strong></h2>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>What is the difference between CM4 and CM4Lite?</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>The CM4Lite variants omit the onboard eMMC flash storage, reducing cost by $5-25 depending on what storage capacity you would have otherwise selected. CM4Lite requires booting from an external source such as a microSD card on your carrier board, USB storage, or network boot. Choose CM4Lite for applications where you need easily swappable storage or when cost optimization is critical. Choose standard CM4 with eMMC for reliability-focused applications where the soldered storage eliminates mechanical failure points.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Can the CM4 boot from NVMe SSD?</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>Yes, but it requires updating the EEPROM bootloader configuration. By default, the CM4 boot order doesn’t include NVMe. Use the rpi-eeprom-config utility to modify the BOOT_ORDER parameter, adding 6 (NVMe) to the sequence. Performance from NVMe significantly exceeds eMMC, with random I/O showing 3x improvements in typical benchmarks. Note that NVMe requires a carrier board with PCIe-to-M.2 routing, which the official IO board provides via its x1 slot (adapter required) or various third-party carrier boards provide directly.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Is the CM4 compatible with Raspberry Pi HATs?</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>The CM4 itself is not directly compatible with HATs, but carrier boards can provide compatibility. The official CM4 IO board includes a standard 40-pin GPIO header that accepts most HATs designed for the Pi 4B. However, HATs that require specific mechanical clearances or use the USB/Ethernet ports in their design may have compatibility issues. When designing custom carrier boards, you can include a 40-pin header to maintain HAT compatibility, or implement the required functionality directly on the carrier board.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>How do I choose between CM4 and Pi 4 Model B?</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>Choose the Pi 4 Model B for standalone projects, education, and applications where you need standard ports immediately available. Choose the <strong>raspberry pi cm4</strong> when: you’re developing a commercial product requiring custom form factor; you need industrial reliability with eMMC storage; you want to expose PCIe for NVMe or expansion cards; you require multiple camera or display interfaces simultaneously; or you need the extended temperature rating for harsh environments. The CM4 plus carrier board approach costs more than a bare Pi 4B but enables possibilities impossible with the standard board.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>What thermal management does the CM4 require?</strong><strong></strong></h3>



<p>The CM4 requires active or passive cooling depending on workload. Under light loads (web server, file sharing), a small heatsink with natural convection suffices. Under sustained heavy loads (video encoding, AI inference), active cooling becomes necessary. The BCM2711 throttles at 80°C, reducing performance to prevent damage. The official IO board includes a PWM-controlled fan header with temperature-based control available through the standard Raspberry Pi cooling daemon. For custom designs, ensure adequate thermal mass and/or airflow for your worst-case workload. Industrial variants rated for higher ambient temperatures may require more aggressive cooling solutions.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Final Thoughts</strong><strong></strong></h2>



<p>The <strong>Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4</strong> represents the culmination of Raspberry Pi’s evolution from educational tool to legitimate industrial computing platform. The combination of modern ARM64 performance, flexible configuration options, exposed PCIe, and the new compact form factor opens applications that previous compute modules couldn’t address.</p>



<p>For hardware developers, the CM4 offers a rare combination: enough processing power for demanding applications, comprehensive interface options, excellent documentation, a vibrant ecosystem of carrier boards and accessories, and pricing that enables experimentation without excessive risk. The ten-year production commitment provides the supply chain confidence that commercial products require.</p>



<p>Whether you’re building your first embedded Linux product or optimizing an existing design, the <strong>raspberry pi cm4</strong> deserves serious consideration. Start with the official IO board to validate your software architecture, then design a custom carrier board optimized for your specific requirements. The extensive reference designs and community support mean you won’t be working in isolation.</p>



<p>The embedded computing landscape continues evolving rapidly, but the CM4 has established itself as a capable, well-supported platform that will remain relevant for years to come. That’s exactly what production hardware development requires.</p>

        if(!wraps.length) return;

            var slider=wrap.querySelector(".pag-slider");
            var track=wrap.querySelector(".pag-track");
            var items=wrap.querySelectorAll(".pag-item");
            var prev=wrap.querySelector(".pag-prev");
            var next=wrap.querySelector(".pag-next");
            var names=wrap.querySelectorAll(".pag-name");
            if(!slider || !track || !items.length || !prev || !next) return;

            function equalizeNames(){
                var max=0;
                names.forEach(function(n){ n.style.height="auto"; });
                names.forEach(function(n){
                    var h=n.offsetHeight;
                    if(h>max) max=h;
                });
                if(max>0){
                    names.forEach(function(n){ n.style.height=max+"px"; });
                }
            }

            function updateButtons(){
                var maxScroll = slider.scrollWidth - slider.clientWidth;
                if(maxScroll < 1){
                    prev.disabled = true;
                    next.disabled = true;
                    return;
                }
                var left = slider.scrollLeft;
                var tol  = 2;
                prev.disabled = left <= tol;
                next.disabled = left >= (maxScroll - tol);
            }

            function step(){
                return slider.clientWidth || 200;
            }

            prev.addEventListener("click",function(){
                slider.scrollBy({left:-step(),behavior:"smooth"});
            });
            next.addEventListener("click",function(){
                slider.scrollBy({left:step(),behavior:"smooth"});
            });

            slider.addEventListener("scroll",updateButtons);
            window.addEventListener("resize",function(){
                equalizeNames();
                updateButtons();
            });

            equalizeNames();
            updateButtons();
        });
    });
